records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֲחִיתֹ֖פֶל אֶל־אַבְשָׁלֹ֑ם אֶבְחֲרָ֣ה נָּ֗א שְׁנֵים־עָשָׂ֥ר אֶ֨לֶף֙ אִ֔ישׁ וְאָק֛וּמָה וְאֶרְדְּפָ֥ה אַחֲרֵי־דָוִ֖ד הַלָּֽיְלָה׃
records.gloss: And said Ahithophel to Absalom, let me choose please twelve thousand men, and I will arise and pursue after David this night.
pieces: Ahithophel said to Absalom, "Let me pick out twelve thousand men, and I will set out and go after David tonight.

L.1: And Ahithophel said to Absalom, "Let me choose, please, twelve thousand men, and I will arise and pursue after David this night.

R.1: Ahithophel said to Absalom, "Let me choose twelve thousand men. I will set out tonight and chase after David.

decisions.choice: let me choose ... I will arise and pursue: Ahithophel offers to lead the attack himself
decisions.reason: All three verbs are first person: Ahithophel asks to pick the men and take command in person. Absalom himself would stay in Jerusalem. Hushai's plan will reverse this and put Absalom at the head of the army (verse 11).

decisions.choice: this night: at once, before David can recover
decisions.reason: David and the people with him had left Jerusalem in haste and arrived worn out (16:14). Ahithophel's whole plan depends on speed: to strike while David is still on the road and has no time to gather troops or cross the Jordan.

decisions.choice: twelve thousand: a picked force, not the whole people
decisions.reason: The number may be meant as a thousand from each of the twelve tribes. The word "thousand" can also name a military unit (see Numbers 1), but the point here is a select, fast-moving force rather than a general call-up.

decisions.choice: go after; chase after
decisions.reason: The verb means to pursue an enemy. Balanced and Readable use everyday words for it.

records.source: וְאָב֣וֹא עָלָ֗יו וְה֤וּא יָגֵ֨עַ֙ וּרְפֵ֣ה יָדַ֔יִם וְהַֽחֲרַדְתִּ֣י אֹת֔וֹ וְנָ֖ס כָּל־הָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר־אִתּ֑וֹ וְהִכֵּיתִ֥י אֶת־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לְבַדּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And I will come upon him and he [is] weary and slack of hands, and I will terrify him, and will flee all the people who [are] with him, and I will strike down the king by himself.
pieces: I will come upon him while he is weary and discouraged and throw him into a panic. All the people with him will run away, and I will strike down the king alone.

L.2: And I will come upon him while he [is] weary and slack of hands, and I will throw him into panic, and all the people who [are] with him will flee, and I will strike down the king alone.

R.2: I will attack him while he is tired and has lost heart. I will make him panic, and all his people will run away. Then I will kill only the king.

decisions.choice: slack of hands: without strength or will to act
decisions.reason: Hands that hang down limp are a picture of losing courage and the will to act (4:1; Isaiah 35:3).

decisions.choice: all the people with him: David's whole company
decisions.reason: The people with David were his fighting men together with their households and the king's household (15:16-18, 22). Ahithophel expects that once the king's party is thrown into panic, they will scatter rather than fight.

decisions.choice: strike down the king alone: only David is to die
decisions.reason: "By himself" stresses that only the king will be killed. Ahithophel is offering Absalom a quick victory with little bloodshed, which would make it easy for the people to accept the new king (verse 3).

decisions.choice: kill
decisions.reason: The verb "strike" here means to strike dead. Readable says so plainly.

records.source: וְאָשִׁ֥יבָה כָל־הָעָ֖ם אֵלֶ֑יךָ כְּשׁ֣וּב הַכֹּ֔ל הָאִישׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתָּ֣ה מְבַקֵּ֔שׁ כָּל־הָעָ֖ם יִהְיֶ֥ה שָׁלֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: And I will bring back all the people to you; as [the] return of the all [is] the man whom you [are] seeking; all the people will be peace.
pieces: Then I will bring all the people back to you. The man you are after is worth the return of them all. All the people will be at peace."

L.3: And I will bring back all the people to you. Like the return of the whole [is] the man whom you [are] seeking; all the people will be [at] peace."

R.3: Then I will bring all the people back to you. If you get the one man you are after, it will be the same as having everyone come back to you. And the whole nation will be at peace."

decisions.choice: like the return of the whole is the man you seek: removing David brings everyone back
alternatives: as a bride returns to her husband; you seek the life of only one man
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is hard to follow word for word: "like the return of the whole is the man whom you are seeking". Taken as it stands, it means that the death of the one man Absalom is after is equal to the return of the whole people to him. An ancient Greek translation reads a fuller text: "as a bride returns to her husband; you are seeking the life of only one man". That reading may preserve words lost from the Hebrew, or it may be the translator's attempt to make sense of the same difficult text. Either way the sense is the same: kill David and the nation will come over to Absalom.

decisions.choice: at peace: unharmed, with no war
decisions.reason: The word means wholeness and safety. With David dead there would be no civil war, and the people would come to Absalom without fighting.

decisions.choice: the man whom you are seeking: David
decisions.reason: Ahithophel does not name David or call him king here. He speaks of him only as the man Absalom wants.

decisions.choice: The man you are after is worth the return of them all; If you get the one man ...
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the comparison in a clear sentence, following the Hebrew text as it stands (see m1).

records.source: וַיִּישַׁ֥ר הַדָּבָ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י אַבְשָׁלֹ֑ם וּבְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל־זִקְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס
records.gloss: And was right the word in [the] eyes of Absalom and in [the] eyes of all [the] elders of Israel.
pieces: The plan seemed right to Absalom and to all the elders of Israel.

L.4: And the word was right in the eyes of Absalom and in the eyes of all the elders of Israel.

R.4: Absalom and all the leaders of Israel thought this plan was a good one.

decisions.choice: was right in the eyes of: seemed right to
decisions.reason: "In the eyes of" means "in the judgment of". The verb means "to be straight, right".

decisions.choice: the elders of Israel: the heads of the tribes and clans
decisions.reason: The elders were the senior men who spoke for the tribes. The elders of Israel had once come to Hebron to make David king (5:3); now they back his son against him.

decisions.choice: leaders
decisions.reason: Readable says "leaders" so that the elders are not taken simply for old men.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אַבְשָׁל֔וֹם קְרָ֣א נָ֔א גַּ֖ם לְחוּשַׁ֣י הָאַרְכִּ֑י וְנִשְׁמְעָ֥ה מַה־בְּפִ֖יו גַּם־הֽוּא׃
records.gloss: And said Absalom, call please also Hushai the Archite, and let us hear what [is] in his mouth, also he.
pieces: But Absalom said, "Call Hushai the Archite as well, and let us hear what he has to say too."

L.5: And Absalom said, "Call, please, Hushai the Archite also, and let us hear what [is] in his mouth, he too."

R.5: But Absalom said, "Call Hushai the Archite too. Let us hear what he says as well."

decisions.choice: Hushai the Archite: David's friend, sent back to work against Ahithophel
decisions.reason: Hushai had come to meet David as he fled, and David sent him back to Jerusalem to pretend to serve Absalom and so defeat Ahithophel's advice (15:32-37). Absalom had accepted him (16:16-19). The Archites were a clan living on the border of Benjamin and Ephraim (Joshua 16:2).

decisions.choice: what is in his mouth: what he has to say
decisions.reason: The mouth stands for a person's speech; Absalom wants to hear Hushai's opinion.

decisions.choice: Absalom asks for a second opinion: the opening David had prayed for
decisions.reason: When David heard that Ahithophel had joined Absalom, he prayed that Yahweh would turn Ahithophel's advice into foolishness (15:31). Absalom's wish to hear Hushai too gives Hushai the chance to do this; the narrator explains it in verse 14.

decisions.choice: But
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable mark the turn: although everyone liked the plan, Absalom still asks for Hushai.

records.heading: Hushai gives his advice

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֣א חוּשַׁי֮ אֶל־אַבְשָׁלוֹם֒ וַיֹּאמֶר֩ אַבְשָׁל֨וֹם אֵלָ֜יו לֵאמֹ֗ר כַּדָּבָ֤ר הַזֶּה֙ דִּבֶּ֣ר אֲחִיתֹ֔פֶל הֲנַעֲשֶׂ֖ה אֶת־דְּבָר֑וֹ אִם־אַ֖יִן אַתָּ֥ה דַבֵּֽר׃ס
records.gloss: And came Hushai to Absalom, and said Absalom to him, saying, According to this word has spoken Ahithophel; shall we do his word? If not, you speak.
pieces: When Hushai came to Absalom, Absalom said to him, "This is what Ahithophel has proposed. Should we do as he says? If not, tell us what you think."

L.6: And Hushai came to Absalom, and Absalom said to him, saying, "Ahithophel has spoken according to this word. Shall we do his word? If not, you speak."

R.6: When Hushai arrived, Absalom told him, "Ahithophel has given us this advice. Should we do what he says? If not, tell us your advice."

decisions.choice: word: what Ahithophel proposed, his plan
decisions.reason: "Word" here means the matter spoken about, Ahithophel's proposal. "Do his word" means carry out his plan.

decisions.choice: according to this word: Absalom repeats the plan to Hushai
decisions.reason: The narrator does not repeat the plan; "this word" stands for Ahithophel's proposal of verses 1-3, which Absalom now sets out for Hushai.

decisions.choice: tell us what you think; tell us your advice
decisions.reason: "You speak" invites Hushai to give his own view; Balanced and Readable say what he is asked to speak about.

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר חוּשַׁ֖י אֶל־אַבְשָׁל֑וֹם לֹֽא־טוֹבָ֧ה הָעֵצָ֛ה אֲשֶׁר־יָעַ֥ץ אֲחִיתֹ֖פֶל בַּפַּ֥עַם הַזֹּֽאת׃
records.gloss: And said Hushai to Absalom, not good [is] the counsel which has counseled Ahithophel at the time this.
pieces: Hushai answered Absalom, "This time the advice Ahithophel has given is not good."

L.7: And Hushai said to Absalom, "Not good [is] the counsel that Ahithophel has counseled this time."

R.7: Hushai told Absalom, "This time Ahithophel's advice is not good."

decisions.choice: this time: unlike his advice at other times
decisions.reason: Hushai grants that Ahithophel's advice is usually good; everyone treated it as if it came from God (16:23). By admitting this he makes his objection sound fair and careful rather than jealous.

decisions.choice: counsel: advice on what to do
decisions.reason: The noun and the verb from the same root run through this story (15:31, 34; 16:20, 23). They mean advice given to a ruler about a course of action.

decisions.choice: advice
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "counsel ... counseled" to show the repeated root; Balanced and Readable use the everyday word "advice".

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר חוּשַׁ֗י אַתָּ֣ה יָ֠דַעְתָּ אֶת־אָבִ֨יךָ וְאֶת־אֲנָשָׁ֜יו כִּ֧י גִבֹּרִ֣ים הֵ֗מָּה וּמָרֵ֥י נֶ֨פֶשׁ֙ הֵ֔מָּה כְּדֹ֥ב שַׁכּ֖וּל בַּשָּׂדֶ֑ה וְאָבִ֨יךָ֙ אִ֣ישׁ מִלְחָמָ֔ה וְלֹ֥א יָלִ֖ין אֶת־הָעָֽם׃
records.gloss: And said Hushai, you know your father and his men, that warriors [are] they and bitter of soul [are] they, like a bear bereaved in the field; and your father [is] a man of war, and not he will spend the night with the people.
pieces: Hushai went on, "You know your father and his men. They are warriors, and they are fierce and enraged, like a bear in the wild robbed of her cubs. Your father is an experienced fighter, and he will not spend the night with the troops.

L.8: And Hushai said, "You know your father and his men, that they [are] mighty men, and they [are] bitter of soul, like a bear robbed of her cubs in the field. And your father [is] a man of war, and he will not spend the night with the people.

R.8: Hushai went on, "You know your father and his men. They are strong fighters, and they are as angry as a mother bear whose cubs have been taken from her. Your father is an experienced soldier. He will not spend the night with his army.

decisions.choice: bitter of soul: fierce and desperate
decisions.reason: The phrase describes people driven to anger or despair, and so dangerous (Judges 18:25; 1 Samuel 22:2). David's men have lost their homes and city and have nothing left to lose.

decisions.choice: a bear robbed of her cubs: a picture of fury
decisions.reason: A mother bear that has lost her young was proverbial for savage anger (Proverbs 17:12; Hosea 13:8).

decisions.choice: he will not spend the night with the people: he will be hidden somewhere apart
decisions.reason: Hushai answers Ahithophel's plan point by point. Ahithophel said he would strike down the king alone (verse 2); Hushai says an experienced soldier like David will not be found sleeping among his men, so a night attack would miss him.

decisions.choice: the people: David's fighting men
decisions.reason: Here "the people" are the troops among whom David might be expected to camp.

decisions.choice: a mother bear whose cubs have been taken from her
decisions.reason: Readable spells out who the bear is and drops "in the field", which only means out in the wild.

decisions.choice: the troops
decisions.reason: Where "the people" means an army in the field, Balanced says "the troops" and Readable "the army".

records.source: הִנֵּ֨ה עַתָּ֤ה הֽוּא־נֶחְבָּא֙ בְּאַחַ֣ת הַפְּחָתִ֔ים א֖וֹ בְּאַחַ֣ד הַמְּקוֹמֹ֑ת וְהָיָ֗ה כִּנְפֹ֤ל בָּהֶם֙ בַּתְּחִלָּ֔ה וְשָׁמַ֤ע הַשֹּׁמֵ֨עַ֙ וְאָמַ֔ר הָֽיְתָה֙ מַגֵּפָ֔ה בָּעָ֕ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר אַחֲרֵ֥י אַבְשָׁלֹֽם׃
records.gloss: Look, now he [is] hidden in one of the pits or in one of the places; and it will be, when falls among them at the first, and will hear the hearer and will say, There has been a slaughter among the people which [is] after Absalom.
pieces: Even now he is hiding in one of the caves or in some other place. When some of the troops fall in the first attack, whoever hears of it will say, 'The troops who follow Absalom have been slaughtered.'

L.9: Look, now he [is] hidden in one of the pits or in one of the places. And it will be, when [some] fall among them at the first, that whoever hears will hear and say, 'There has been a slaughter among the people who follow Absalom.'

R.9: Even now he is hiding in a cave or some other place. If some of your soldiers are killed in the first fight, people will hear about it. They will say, 'Absalom's army is being slaughtered!'

decisions.choice: when some fall among them at first: Absalom's men suffer losses in the first clash
alternatives: when he falls upon them at the first
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "when falling among them at the first". It may mean "when some of them fall", that is, some of Absalom's men, or "when he falls upon them", that is, when David attacks them from his hiding place. Either way the first fighting goes badly for Absalom's side, and the news spreads.

decisions.choice: pits: caves or holes in the ground
decisions.reason: The word means a pit or hollow. In the hill country east of Jerusalem there were many caves where a man could hide, as David had done when he fled from Saul (1 Samuel 22:1; 24:4).

decisions.choice: whoever hears will hear: the rumor will spread
decisions.reason: "The one hearing will hear" means that anyone at all who hears the news will pass it on. Hushai warns that a small setback would be reported as a disaster.

decisions.choice: slaughter: a heavy defeat
decisions.reason: The word is used of a plague or of a crushing defeat in battle (18:7; 1 Samuel 4:17).

decisions.choice: your soldiers
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear whose men fall, taking the reading in m1; the other reading would still mean losses for Absalom's side.

records.source: וְה֣וּא גַם־בֶּן־חַ֗יִל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לִבּ֛וֹ כְּלֵ֥ב הָאַרְיֵ֖ה הִמֵּ֣ס יִמָּ֑ס כִּֽי־יֹדֵ֤עַ כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ כִּי־גִבּ֣וֹר אָבִ֔יךָ וּבְנֵי־חַ֖יִל אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And he also, a son of strength whose heart [is] like the heart of the lion, surely will melt; for knows all Israel that a warrior [is] your father and sons of strength [are] who [are] with him.
pieces: Then even the bravest man, whose heart is like a lion's, will lose all courage, for all Israel knows that your father is a warrior and that the men with him are brave.

L.10: And even he [who is] a son of strength, whose heart [is] like the heart of the lion, will utterly melt; for all Israel knows that your father [is] a mighty man, and those who [are] with him [are] sons of strength.

R.10: Then even your bravest soldiers, who have hearts like lions, will be terrified. Everyone in Israel knows that your father is a great fighter and that his men are brave.

decisions.choice: will utterly melt: will lose all courage
decisions.reason: A melting heart is a picture of courage draining away in fear (Joshua 2:11; 7:5). The verb is doubled for emphasis.

decisions.choice: son of strength: a brave, capable man
decisions.reason: "Son of" a quality describes someone marked by it. The same phrase in the plural describes David's men at the end of the verse.

decisions.choice: even he: the bravest on Absalom's side
decisions.reason: Hushai means that if the first attack fails, even Absalom's boldest fighters will lose heart, because they know whom they are fighting.

decisions.choice: your bravest soldiers
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plural and says whose soldiers are meant, since the Hebrew "he" stands for any such man on Absalom's side.

records.source: כִּ֣י יָעַ֗צְתִּי הֵ֠אָסֹף יֵאָסֵ֨ף עָלֶ֤יךָ כָל־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מִדָּן֙ וְעַד־בְּאֵ֣ר שֶׁ֔בַע כַּח֥וֹל אֲשֶׁר־עַל־הַיָּ֖ם לָרֹ֑ב וּפָנֶ֥יךָ הֹלְכִ֖ים בַּקְרָֽב׃
records.gloss: For I counsel: let be gathered fully to you all Israel from Dan and to Beersheba, like the sand which [is] by the sea for multitude, and your face going in battle.
pieces: So my advice is this: let all Israel be gathered to you, from Dan to Beersheba, as many as the sand by the sea, and lead them into battle yourself.

L.11: But I counsel: let all Israel be fully gathered to you, from Dan even to Beersheba, like the sand that [is] by the sea for multitude, and your face going into battle.

R.11: Here is my advice. Bring together all Israel, from Dan in the far north to Beersheba in the far south. Then you will have as many men as there are grains of sand on the seashore. And go into battle with them yourself.

decisions.choice: from Dan to Beersheba: the whole land, from north to south
decisions.reason: Dan was the northernmost town of Israel and Beersheba the southernmost; the phrase means the entire nation (3:10; 1 Samuel 3:20).

decisions.choice: your face going into battle: you yourself leading the army
decisions.reason: "Your face" means "you in person" (compare Exodus 33:14). Ahithophel had offered to lead a small force himself (verse 1); Hushai flatters Absalom by urging him to lead the whole nation in person. An ancient Greek translation reads "your face going in their midst", with the same sense.

decisions.choice: like the sand by the sea: a vast number
decisions.reason: The picture is used of the countless descendants promised to Abraham (Genesis 22:17) and of huge armies (Judges 7:12; 1 Samuel 13:5).

decisions.choice: fully gathered: a general call-up, which takes time
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis. Gathering the whole nation would take days, which is exactly the time David needs to escape and organize (verses 16, 22).

decisions.choice: in the far north ... in the far south
decisions.reason: Readable explains where Dan and Beersheba lay so that the phrase can be understood, as in 3:10.

decisions.choice: lead them into battle yourself
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of the idiom "your face going" (see m2).

records.source: וּבָ֣אנוּ אֵלָ֗יו בְּאַחַ֤ד הַמְּקוֹמֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִמְצָ֣א שָׁ֔ם וְנַ֣חְנוּ עָלָ֔יו כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר יִפֹּ֥ל הַטַּ֖ל עַל־הָאֲדָמָ֑ה וְלֹֽא־נ֥וֹתַר בּ֛וֹ וּבְכָל־הָאֲנָשִׁ֥ים אֲשֶׁר־אִתּ֖וֹ גַּם־אֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: And we will come to him in one of the places where he is found there, and we [will] settle on him as falls the dew on the ground; and not will be left of him and of all the men who [are] with him even one.
pieces: Then we will come upon him wherever he may be found and settle on him the way dew falls on the ground. Neither he nor any of the men with him will be left, not even one.

L.12: And we will come to him in one of the places where he is found, and we will settle on him as the dew falls on the ground; and there will not be left of him and of all the men who [are] with him even one.

R.12: We will find him wherever he is, and we will come down on him the way dew covers the ground. Not one of them will be left alive, not David and not any of his men.

decisions.choice: we will settle on him: we will come down and cover him
decisions.reason: The verb means to come to rest on something. Like the dew, the army will settle on every place at once.

decisions.choice: as dew falls on the ground: everywhere, silently, with no escape
decisions.reason: Dew covers the whole ground and leaves no spot untouched. Hushai's picture answers Ahithophel's: instead of a quick strike at one man, a host so large that no one can slip away.

decisions.choice: not even one will be left: David and all his men destroyed
decisions.reason: Hushai's plan sounds bolder than Ahithophel's, who wanted only the king to die (verse 2), and so appeals to Absalom's pride.

decisions.choice: left alive; not David
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that "left" means left alive and names David for "him".

records.source: וְאִם־אֶל־עִיר֙ יֵֽאָסֵ֔ף וְהִשִּׂ֧יאוּ כָֽל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶל־הָעִ֥יר הַהִ֖יא חֲבָלִ֑ים וְסָחַ֤בְנוּ אֹתוֹ֙ עַד־הַנַּ֔חַל עַ֛ד אֲשֶֽׁר־לֹא־נִמְצָ֥א שָׁ֖ם גַּם־צְרֽוֹר׃פ
records.gloss: And if into a city he is gathered, then will bring all Israel to the city that ropes, and we will drag it to the wadi until that not is found there even a pebble.
pieces: If he pulls back into a town, all Israel will haul ropes up to it, and we will drag the whole place down into the valley until not even a pebble is left there."

L.13: And if he is gathered into a city, then all Israel will bring ropes to that city, and we will drag it into the valley until not even a pebble is found there."

R.13: And if David goes into a town to hide, all Israel will bring ropes, and we will pull the whole town down into the valley. Not even a small stone will be left there!"

decisions.choice: drag it into the valley with ropes: an exaggeration of overwhelming strength
decisions.reason: No army could pull a walled town down with ropes. Hushai paints a boastful picture to show that, with all Israel behind him, Absalom could not fail.

decisions.choice: valley: a wadi, a stream bed below the town
decisions.reason: The word names a valley with a stream that runs in the rainy season. Towns were often built on hills above such valleys.

decisions.choice: gathered into a city: withdraws to a walled town
decisions.reason: The verb is the same one used in verse 11 for gathering all Israel. If David "gathers himself" into a town, all Israel gathered against him will still crush him.

decisions.choice: David; to hide
decisions.reason: Readable names David for "he" and says why he would go into a town.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ וְכָל־אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל טוֹבָ֗ה עֲצַת֙ חוּשַׁ֣י הָאַרְכִּ֔י מֵעֲצַ֖ת אֲחִיתֹ֑פֶל וַיהוָ֣ה צִוָּ֗ה לְהָפֵ֞ר אֶת־עֲצַ֤ת אֲחִיתֹ֨פֶל֙ הַטּוֹבָ֔ה לְבַעֲב֗וּר הָבִ֧יא יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־אַבְשָׁל֖וֹם אֶת־הָרָעָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And said Absalom and every man of Israel, better [is the] counsel of Hushai the Archite than [the] counsel of Ahithophel. And Yahweh had commanded to frustrate the counsel of Ahithophel the good, in order to bring Yahweh to Absalom the disaster.
pieces: Then Absalom and all the men of Israel declared, "Hushai the Archite gives better advice than Ahithophel." For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had decreed that Ahithophel's good advice would be defeated, so that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} could bring disaster on Absalom.

L.14: And Absalom and every man of Israel said, "The counsel of Hushai the Archite [is] better than the counsel of Ahithophel." And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded to frustrate the good counsel of Ahithophel, in order that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} might bring the disaster on Absalom.

R.14: Absalom and all the men of Israel said, "Hushai's advice is better than Ahithophel's." This happened because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had decided to make Ahithophel's good advice fail. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was going to bring disaster on Absalom.

decisions.choice: Yahweh had commanded to frustrate the good counsel: Yahweh was at work through the choices of the men in the council
decisions.reason: The narrator steps out of the story to say what the people in it could not see. Ahithophel's advice was in fact good, and Absalom and his men chose freely, yet Yahweh had decided beforehand that it would come to nothing. This is the answer to David's prayer, "Yahweh, turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness" (15:31), and to the mission he gave Hushai (15:34). The same hidden working of Yahweh through human decisions appears in 1 Kings 12:15 and Proverbs 21:30; 19:21.

decisions.choice: commanded: decreed, determined
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to give an order. With Yahweh as the subject and an action as the object, it means that he decreed what would happen (Psalm 133:3; Lamentations 1:17).

decisions.choice: frustrate: break, bring to nothing
decisions.reason: The verb means to break or annul. It is the word David used when he sent Hushai back: "you will frustrate for me the counsel of Ahithophel" (15:34).

decisions.choice: the disaster: ruin, not moral evil
decisions.reason: The noun can mean evil, harm or calamity. Here it is the ruin that will come on Absalom in battle (18:9-15). The article points to that particular disaster.

decisions.choice: and Yahweh had commanded: the narrator's explanation
decisions.reason: The sentence puts "Yahweh" first, before the verb, which marks a comment outside the flow of events, giving the reason behind what happened.

decisions.choice: had decreed that ... would be defeated; had decided to make ... fail
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "decreed" or "decided" because "commanded" with no one being ordered sounds odd in English; see m2.

decisions.choice: advice
decisions.reason: As in verse 7.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר חוּשַׁ֗י אֶל־צָד֤וֹק וְאֶל־אֶבְיָתָר֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים כָּזֹ֣את וְכָזֹ֗את יָעַ֤ץ אֲחִיתֹ֨פֶל֙ אֶת־אַבְשָׁלֹ֔ם וְאֵ֖ת זִקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְכָזֹ֥את וְכָזֹ֖את יָעַ֥צְתִּי אָֽנִי׃
records.gloss: And said Hushai to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, like this and like this counseled Ahithophel Absalom and [the] elders of Israel, and like this and like this counseled I.
pieces: Hushai told Zadok and Abiathar the priests, "Ahithophel advised Absalom and the elders of Israel to do this and that, but I advised this and that.

L.15: And Hushai said to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, "Thus and thus Ahithophel counseled Absalom and the elders of Israel, and thus and thus I myself counseled.

R.15: Then Hushai told the priests Zadok and Abiathar, "Ahithophel gave Absalom and the leaders of Israel this advice, but I gave them different advice.

decisions.choice: thus and thus: such and such
decisions.reason: The narrator does not repeat the two plans the reader already knows; "thus and thus" stands for them.

decisions.choice: Zadok and Abiathar the priests: David's allies in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: David had sent the two priests back to Jerusalem with the ark, so that Hushai could pass on what he heard through them and their sons (15:27-29, 35-36).

decisions.choice: I myself counseled: an added pronoun for emphasis
decisions.reason: The pronoun "I" is added after the verb, setting Hushai's advice against Ahithophel's.

decisions.choice: the leaders of Israel
decisions.reason: As in verse 4.

records.heading: David is warned

records.source: וְעַתָּ֡ה שִׁלְח֣וּ מְהֵרָה֩ וְהַגִּ֨ידוּ לְדָוִ֜ד לֵאמֹ֗ר אַל־תָּ֤לֶן הַלַּ֨יְלָה֙ בְּעַֽרְב֣וֹת הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר וְגַ֖ם עָב֣וֹר תַּעֲב֑וֹר פֶּ֚ן יְבֻלַּ֣ע לַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וּלְכָל־הָעָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And now send quickly and tell to David, saying, do not spend the night this night in [the] plains of the wilderness, and also surely cross over, lest it be swallowed up for the king and for all the people who [are] with him.
pieces: Now send word quickly and tell David, 'Do not camp tonight in the plains by the wilderness. Cross over without fail, or the king and all the people with him will be wiped out.'"

L.16: And now send quickly and tell David, saying, 'Do not spend the night tonight in the plains of the wilderness, but be sure to cross over, lest the king and all the people who [are] with him be swallowed up.'"

R.16: Now quickly send a message to David. Tell him, 'Do not stay tonight in the open country near the desert. Cross the river right away, or you and all your people will be destroyed!'"

decisions.choice: the plains of the wilderness
decisions.reason: The reading the scribes marked for reading aloud is "the plains", the low open land by the Jordan. The consonants written in the text could also be read "the fords", the river crossings. The same difference occurs at 15:28. Either way David is camped by the Jordan on the wilderness side.

decisions.choice: be sure to cross over: the verb is doubled for urgency
decisions.reason: Hushai cannot be certain that Absalom will hold to his advice; Ahithophel's plan could still be taken up. So David must not stay on the near side of the Jordan for even one night.

decisions.choice: be swallowed up: be utterly destroyed
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is impersonal, "lest it be swallowed up for the king". To be swallowed up means to be wiped out completely (Lamentations 2:2, 5).

decisions.choice: you and all your people
decisions.reason: Hushai's message speaks of "the king" in the third person, as courtiers did. Readable has it address David directly.

decisions.choice: Cross the river
decisions.reason: Readable names what David is to cross: the Jordan (verse 22).

records.source: וִיהוֹנָתָ֨ן וַאֲחִימַ֜עַץ עֹמְדִ֣ים בְּעֵין־רֹגֵ֗ל וְהָלְכָ֤ה הַשִּׁפְחָה֙ וְהִגִּ֣ידָה לָהֶ֔ם וְהֵם֙ יֵֽלְכ֔וּ וְהִגִּ֖ידוּ לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֑ד כִּ֣י לֹ֥א יוּכְל֛וּ לְהֵרָא֖וֹת לָב֥וֹא הָעִֽירָה׃
records.gloss: And Jonathan and Ahimaaz [were] standing at En-rogel, and would go the maidservant and would tell them, and they would go and would tell King David; for not they were able to be seen to come into the city.
pieces: Jonathan and Ahimaaz were waiting at En-rogel. A servant girl would go and pass the news to them, and they would go and tell King David, because they could not risk being seen entering the city.

L.17: And Jonathan and Ahimaaz [were] staying at En-rogel, and the servant girl would go and tell them, and they would go and tell King David, for they could not be seen coming into the city.

R.17: Jonathan and Ahimaaz were waiting at En-rogel, a spring just outside Jerusalem. A servant girl would go and give them the news, and then they would go and tell King David. They could not go into the city, because someone might see them.

decisions.choice: Jonathan and Ahimaaz: the sons of the two priests
decisions.reason: Jonathan was Abiathar's son and Ahimaaz was Zadok's son. David had named them as the messengers who would bring him news (15:27, 36).

decisions.choice: En-rogel: a spring just outside Jerusalem
decisions.reason: En-rogel was a spring in the valley south-east of the city, on the border between Judah and Benjamin (Joshua 15:7; 18:16; 1 Kings 1:9).

decisions.choice: would go ... would tell: the arrangement the messengers worked by
decisions.reason: The verb forms describe a plan set up in advance, or a practice repeated, rather than one event. A servant girl going out of the city, perhaps to fetch water at the spring, would draw no attention.

decisions.choice: servant girl: a female servant
decisions.reason: The word names a woman servant of a household. The text does not say whose household she belonged to.

decisions.choice: a spring just outside Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Readable explains what En-rogel was and so why the young men could wait there.

records.source: וַיַּ֤רְא אֹתָם֙ נַ֔עַר וַיַּגֵּ֖ד לְאַבְשָׁלֹ֑ם וַיֵּלְכוּ֩ שְׁנֵיהֶ֨ם מְהֵרָ֜ה וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ׀אֶל־בֵּֽית־אִ֣ישׁ בְּבַחוּרִ֗ים וְל֥וֹ בְאֵ֛ר בַּחֲצֵר֖וֹ וַיֵּ֥רְדוּ שָֽׁם׃
records.gloss: And saw them a young man and told Absalom; and went the two of them quickly and came to [the] house of a man in Bahurim, and to him [was] a well in his courtyard, and they went down there.
pieces: But a young man spotted them and told Absalom. So the two hurried off to Bahurim, to the house of a man whose courtyard had a well, and they climbed down into it.

L.18: But a young man saw them and told Absalom. And the two of them went quickly and came to the house of a man in Bahurim, and he [had] a well in his courtyard, and they went down there.

R.18: But a young man saw them and reported it to Absalom. So the two of them hurried away to the village of Bahurim. A man there had a well in his courtyard, and the two young men let themselves down into it to hide.

decisions.choice: Bahurim: a village on the road from Jerusalem to the Jordan
decisions.reason: Bahurim lay just east of the Mount of Olives. It was Shimei's home, where he cursed David (16:5); here a household in the same village helps David's men.

decisions.choice: well: a shaft dug in the ground, here probably dry
decisions.reason: The word normally names a well dug down to water. Since two men could hide in this one, it was probably dry or nearly so, perhaps a cistern for storing rainwater.

decisions.choice: a young man: a boy or a servant
decisions.reason: The word can mean a youth or a young servant. Who he was, the text does not say; he was on Absalom's side.

decisions.choice: climbed down into it
decisions.reason: "Went down there" means into the well itself, as verse 21 shows.

decisions.choice: to hide
decisions.reason: Readable says why they went down into the well.

records.source: וַתִּקַּ֣ח הָאִשָּׁ֗ה וַתִּפְרֹ֤שׂ אֶת־הַמָּסָךְ֙ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י הַבְּאֵ֔ר וַתִּשְׁטַ֥ח עָלָ֖יו הָֽרִפ֑וֹת וְלֹ֥א נוֹדַ֖ע דָּבָֽר׃
records.gloss: And took the woman and spread the covering over [the] face of the well, and spread on it the groats, and not was known a thing.
pieces: The woman of the house took a covering, spread it over the mouth of the well, and scattered grain on it, so that nothing could be seen.

L.19: And the woman took the covering and spread [it] over the face of the well, and scattered the groats on it, and nothing was known.

R.19: The woman of the house took a cover and spread it over the opening of the well. Then she scattered grain on top of it, so no one could tell that anything was there.

decisions.choice: groats: crushed or husked grain
decisions.reason: The word is rare (elsewhere only Proverbs 27:22) and seems to mean grain that has been crushed or pounded. Grain spread out to dry in a courtyard was an everyday sight.

decisions.choice: the covering: a cloth or screen
decisions.reason: The noun names something spread to cover or screen, the same word used of the curtain at the entrance of the tabernacle (Exodus 26:36).

decisions.choice: the woman: the wife of the house
decisions.reason: "The woman" is the woman of the house where the men hid, most likely the householder's wife. Like Rahab with the spies (Joshua 2:4-6), she hides the messengers.

decisions.choice: The woman of the house
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear which woman is meant.

decisions.choice: nothing could be seen; no one could tell that anything was there
decisions.reason: "Nothing was known" means the hiding place could not be detected.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ עַבְדֵי֩ אַבְשָׁל֨וֹם אֶֽל־הָאִשָּׁ֜ה הַבַּ֗יְתָה וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ אַיֵּ֗ה אֲחִימַ֨עַץ֙ וִיה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן וַתֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה עָבְר֖וּ מִיכַ֣ל הַמָּ֑יִם וַיְבַקְשׁוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א מָצָ֔אוּ וַיָּשֻׁ֖בוּ יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And came [the] servants of Absalom to the woman to the house and said, where [are] Ahimaaz and Jonathan? And said to them the woman, they have crossed [the] stream of the water. And they searched and not found, and they returned [to] Jerusalem.
pieces: Absalom's servants came to the house and asked the woman, "Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?" The woman told them, "They have gone across the stream." They searched but could not find them, so they went back to Jerusalem.

L.20: And Absalom's servants came to the woman at the house and said, "Where [are] Ahimaaz and Jonathan?" And the woman said to them, "They have crossed the stream of water." And they searched and did not find [them], and they returned [to] Jerusalem.

R.20: Absalom's servants came to the house and asked the woman, "Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?" She answered, "They went across the stream." The men looked for them but could not find them, so they went back to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: the stream of water: meaning uncertain
decisions.reason: The first word occurs only here. It may mean a small stream or channel of water, perhaps a brook near Bahurim. Some take it as the edge of the water, the Jordan itself; others think it is a place name. The woman's point is clear: the men have gone on beyond reach.

decisions.choice: the woman sends the searchers away: like Rahab
decisions.reason: Like Rahab, who hid the spies on her roof and sent the king's men off in the wrong direction (Joshua 2:4-7), and like Michal, who misled Saul's men to save David (1 Samuel 19:12-17), this woman protects David's messengers by misleading his enemies. The text tells what she did without comment.

decisions.choice: Absalom's servants: men sent by the new king
decisions.reason: The servants of a king are his officials and agents; here they are the men Absalom sent to catch the messengers.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep "servants" here: these are not court officials but men carrying out Absalom's orders.

records.source: וַיְהִ֣י׀אַחֲרֵ֣י לֶכְתָּ֗ם וַֽיַּעֲלוּ֙ מֵֽהַבְּאֵ֔ר וַיֵּ֣לְכ֔וּ וַיַּגִּ֖דוּ לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֑ד וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֶל־דָּוִ֗ד ק֣וּמוּ וְעִבְר֤וּ מְהֵרָה֙ אֶת־הַמַּ֔יִם כִּי־כָ֛כָה יָעַ֥ץ עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם אֲחִיתֹֽפֶל׃
records.gloss: And it was after their going, and they came up from the well and went and told King David, and said to David, arise and cross quickly the water, for thus has counseled against you Ahithophel.
pieces: After the men had left, the two climbed out of the well and went to tell King David. They said to David, "Get up and cross the water at once, for this is what Ahithophel has advised against you."

L.21: And it was after they had gone, that they came up from the well and went and told King David, and they said to David, "Arise and cross the water quickly, for thus Ahithophel has counseled against you."

R.21: After Absalom's men left, Jonathan and Ahimaaz climbed out of the well and went to report to King David. They told him, "Hurry and get across the river now! Ahithophel has given advice to attack you."

decisions.choice: thus Ahithophel has counseled against you: they report the danger, Ahithophel's plan
decisions.reason: The messengers speak of Ahithophel's plan for a quick night attack, not of Hushai's, because that was the danger to be escaped: Absalom might yet change his mind (verse 16). "Against you" is plural, meaning David and the people with him.

decisions.choice: the water: the Jordan
decisions.reason: "The water" is the river Jordan, which David's company crosses in the next verse.

decisions.choice: Absalom's men; Jonathan and Ahimaaz
decisions.reason: Readable names who left and who came up, since the Hebrew uses only "they" for both groups.

decisions.choice: the river
decisions.reason: Readable says "river" so that the reader knows which water is meant (see m2).

records.source: וַיָּ֣קָם דָּוִ֗ד וְכָל־הָעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֔וֹ וַיַּעַבְר֖וּ אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן עַד־א֣וֹר הַבֹּ֗קֶר עַד־אַחַד֙ לֹ֣א נֶעְדָּ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־עָבַ֖ר אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃
records.gloss: And arose David and all the people who [were] with him, and they crossed the Jordan; until [the] light of the morning, until one not was missing who not had crossed the Jordan.
pieces: So David and all the people with him set out and crossed the Jordan. By daybreak not a single one was left who had not crossed the Jordan.

L.22: And David arose, and all the people who [were] with him, and they crossed the Jordan. By the light of the morning not one was missing who had not crossed the Jordan.

R.22: So David and all his people got up and crossed the Jordan River. By sunrise every one of them was across.

decisions.choice: not one was missing who had not crossed: all of them crossed
decisions.reason: The Hebrew piles up negatives for emphasis: "until one, not was missing who had not crossed". It means that every last person was over the river before dawn.

decisions.choice: crossed the Jordan: out of immediate reach
decisions.reason: With the river between them and Jerusalem, David's company was safe from a sudden night attack and could move on to Mahanaim (verse 24).

decisions.choice: every one of them was across
decisions.reason: Readable turns the double negative into a plain positive statement.

records.source: וַאֲחִיתֹ֣פֶל רָאָ֗ה כִּ֣י לֹ֣א נֶעֶשְׂתָה֮ עֲצָתוֹ֒ וַיַּחֲבֹ֣שׁ אֶֽת־הַחֲמ֗וֹר וַיָּ֜קָם וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ אֶל־בֵּיתוֹ֙ אֶל־עִיר֔וֹ וַיְצַ֥ו אֶל־בֵּית֖וֹ וַיֵּחָנַ֑ק וַיָּ֕מָת וַיִּקָּבֵ֖ר בְּקֶ֥בֶר אָבִֽיו׃ס
records.gloss: And Ahithophel saw that not was done his counsel, and he saddled the donkey and arose and went to his house, to his city; and he gave orders to his house and strangled himself and died, and was buried in [the] tomb of his father.
pieces: Ahithophel saw that his advice had not been carried out. He saddled his donkey and set off for home, to his own town. He put his household in order and then hanged himself. So he died, and they buried him in his father's tomb.

L.23: And Ahithophel saw that his counsel had not been done, and he saddled the donkey and arose and went to his house, to his city. And he gave orders to his house, and he hanged himself and died, and he was buried in the tomb of his father.

R.23: Ahithophel saw that Absalom had not taken his advice. So he saddled his donkey and went back home to his own town. He gave orders about his family and property, and then he hanged himself. He died and was buried in his father's tomb.

decisions.choice: Ahithophel saw that his counsel had not been done: he foresaw the end
decisions.reason: The text gives no reason for what he did next beyond this. The story implies that Ahithophel saw that Absalom's cause was now lost, and that as David's adviser who had turned against him he could expect no mercy.

decisions.choice: gave orders to his house: set his affairs in order
decisions.reason: The phrase means giving final instructions to one's household before death (2 Kings 20:1; Isaiah 38:1).

decisions.choice: his city: Giloh
decisions.reason: Ahithophel came from Giloh in the hill country of Judah (15:12).

decisions.choice: hanged himself: the end of the betrayer
decisions.reason: The verb means to strangle oneself. Ahithophel, the trusted friend who turned against David (compare Psalm 41:10; 55:13-15), dies by his own hand. The early Greek translation of this verse uses the same verb that Matthew 27:5 uses of Judas.

decisions.choice: buried in his father's tomb: an ordinary family burial
decisions.reason: Families were buried together in a family tomb. Ahithophel is buried with his father in the normal way; the text passes no further judgment.

decisions.choice: Absalom had not taken
decisions.reason: Readable supplies who did not follow the advice, since the Hebrew uses a passive.

decisions.choice: put his household in order
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of the idiom (see m2).

records.source: וְדָוִ֖ד בָּ֣א מַחֲנָ֑יְמָה וְאַבְשָׁלֹ֗ם עָבַר֙ אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן ה֕וּא וְכָל־אִ֥ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עִמּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And David had come to Mahanaim, and Absalom had crossed the Jordan, he and every man of Israel with him.
pieces: David had reached Mahanaim by the time Absalom crossed the Jordan with all the men of Israel.

L.24: And David had come to Mahanaim, and Absalom had crossed the Jordan, he and every man of Israel with him.

R.24: David arrived at the town of Mahanaim. Meanwhile Absalom and all the army of Israel crossed the Jordan River.

decisions.choice: David had come ... Absalom had crossed: two events side by side
decisions.reason: Both clauses put the subject first, which sets the two movements side by side: David was already in Mahanaim when Absalom crossed after him.

decisions.choice: Mahanaim: a town east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Mahanaim lay in Gilead, east of the Jordan. It had been the capital of Saul's son Ishbosheth (2:8-9).

decisions.choice: every man of Israel: the army Absalom raised
decisions.reason: Absalom followed Hushai's advice and gathered all Israel (verse 11). "Every man of Israel" here is the fighting force of the tribes that followed him.

decisions.choice: all the army of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says "army" because these are the men gathered to fight (see m3).

records.heading: David at Mahanaim

records.source: וְאֶת־עֲמָשָׂ֗א שָׂ֧ם אַבְשָׁלֹ֛ם תַּ֥חַת יוֹאָ֖ב עַל־הַצָּבָ֑א וַעֲמָשָׂ֣א בֶן־אִ֗ישׁ וּשְׁמוֹ֙ יִתְרָ֣א הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִ֔י אֲשֶׁר־בָּא֙ אֶל־אֲבִיגַ֣ל בַּת־נָחָ֔שׁ אֲח֥וֹת צְרוּיָ֖ה אֵ֥ם יוֹאָֽב׃
records.gloss: And Amasa had set Absalom instead of Joab over the army; and Amasa [was the] son of a man and his name [was] Ithra the Israelite, who had gone into Abigail daughter of Nahash, sister of Zeruiah, mother of Joab.
pieces: Absalom had put Amasa in command of the army instead of Joab. Amasa's father was a man named Ithra the Israelite, who had slept with Abigail daughter of Nahash, the sister of Zeruiah, Joab's mother.

L.25: And Absalom had set Amasa over the army in place of Joab. And Amasa [was the] son of a man whose name [was] Ithra the Israelite, who had gone in to Abigail daughter of Nahash, sister of Zeruiah, Joab's mother.

R.25: Absalom had made Amasa commander of his army in place of Joab. Amasa's father was a man named Ithra the Israelite. His mother was Abigail, who was the daughter of Nahash and the sister of Zeruiah, Joab's mother. So Amasa and Joab were cousins.

decisions.choice: the Israelite
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text here calls Ithra "the Israelite". The list in 1 Chronicles 2:17 calls him "Jether the Ishmaelite", and some manuscripts of the early Greek translation of Samuel read "the Jezreelite". Calling a man in Israel "the Israelite" would be strange unless it set him apart from something else, so the Chronicles reading may be the original; the Hebrew text of Samuel is followed here.

decisions.choice: Abigail daughter of Nahash, sister of Zeruiah: David's half-sister
alternatives: daughter of Nahash, as her mother's name
decisions.reason: 1 Chronicles 2:13-17 lists Zeruiah and Abigail as sisters of David, daughters of Jesse. Here their parent is Nahash. Nahash may have been their mother, or their father before their mother married Jesse; the text does not explain. Either way Amasa and Joab were cousins and both nephews of David.

decisions.choice: had gone in to: had sexual relations with
decisions.reason: "Go in to" a woman is a common way of speaking of sexual union, used both of marriage (Genesis 29:21) and of other relationships. The text does not say whether Ithra and Abigail were married.

decisions.choice: over the army: commander of the army
decisions.reason: Joab, son of Zeruiah, was David's commander of the army (8:16). Absalom replaces him with Joab's own cousin; the two will meet again in 19:14 and 20:8-10.

decisions.choice: So Amasa and Joab were cousins
decisions.reason: Readable states the family link the verse is giving, since the list of names is hard to follow.

decisions.choice: had slept with
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a plain expression that, like the Hebrew, does not say whether they were married (see m3).

records.source: וַיִּ֤חַן יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְאַבְשָׁלֹ֔ם אֶ֖רֶץ הַגִּלְעָֽד׃ס
records.gloss: And encamped Israel and Absalom [in the] land of Gilead.
pieces: Israel and Absalom made camp in the land of Gilead.

L.26: And Israel and Absalom encamped [in] the land of Gilead.

R.26: Absalom and the army of Israel set up camp in the region of Gilead.

decisions.choice: Israel: the men of the tribes who followed Absalom
decisions.reason: "Israel" here is Absalom's army, "every man of Israel" of verse 24.

decisions.choice: the land of Gilead: the hill country east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Gilead was the region east of the Jordan where Mahanaim lay (verse 24); Absalom camps close to David.

decisions.choice: the army of Israel
decisions.reason: As in verse 24.

records.source: וַיְהִ֕י כְּב֥וֹא דָוִ֖ד מַחֲנָ֑יְמָה וְשֹׁבִ֨י בֶן־נָחָ֜שׁ מֵרַבַּ֣ת בְּנֵֽי־עַמּ֗וֹן וּמָכִ֤יר בֶּן־עַמִּיאֵל֙ מִלֹּ֣א דְבָ֔ר וּבַרְזִלַּ֥י הַגִּלְעָדִ֖י מֵרֹגְלִֽים׃
records.gloss: And it was when came David to Mahanaim, and Shobi son of Nahash from Rabbah of [the] sons of Ammon, and Machir son of Ammiel from Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim,
pieces: When David came to Mahanaim, Shobi son of Nahash from Rabbah of the Ammonites, Machir son of Ammiel from Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim

L.27: And it was, when David came to Mahanaim, that Shobi son of Nahash from Rabbah of the sons of Ammon, and Machir son of Ammiel from Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim,

R.27: When David came to Mahanaim, three men came to help him. They were Shobi son of Nahash from the Ammonite city of Rabbah, Machir son of Ammiel from Lo-debar, and Barzillai from Rogelim in Gilead.

decisions.choice: one sentence across verses 27-29
decisions.reason: The names in verse 27 are the subject of the verb "brought" at the end of the list in verse 29; the whole is one sentence.

decisions.choice: Shobi son of Nahash: a son of the Ammonite king
decisions.reason: Nahash had been king of the Ammonites and had shown David kindness (10:1-2). His son Hanun insulted David's envoys, and David later took Rabbah, the Ammonite capital (12:26-31). Shobi, another son of Nahash, now comes to David's aid; he may have been ruling Rabbah under David. This Nahash is probably a different person from the Nahash of verse 25.

decisions.choice: Machir son of Ammiel from Lo-debar: the man who had sheltered Mephibosheth
decisions.reason: Machir had given a home to Jonathan's son Mephibosheth until David brought him to Jerusalem (9:4-5).

decisions.choice: Barzillai the Gileadite: a rich old man of Gilead
decisions.reason: Barzillai was a very old and wealthy man; David later wished to reward him at court (19:32-40; 1 Kings 2:7).

decisions.choice: three men came to help him
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long Hebrew sentence into shorter ones and supplies a verb so that the first can stand on its own; the gifts follow in verses 28-29.

records.source: מִשְׁכָּ֤ב וְסַפּוֹת֙ וּכְלִ֣י יוֹצֵ֔ר וְחִטִּ֥ים וּשְׂעֹרִ֖ים וְקֶ֣מַח וְקָלִ֑י וּפ֥וֹל וַעֲדָשִׁ֖ים וְקָלִֽי׃
records.gloss: Bedding and basins and vessels of [the] potter, and wheat and barley and flour and roasted grain, and beans and lentils and roasted grain,
pieces: brought bedding, basins and clay pots, and wheat and barley, flour and roasted grain, beans and lentils,

L.28: bedding and basins and potter's vessels, and wheat and barley and flour and roasted grain, and beans and lentils and roasted grain,

R.28: They brought beds, bowls and clay pots. They also brought wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans and lentils.

decisions.choice: roasted grain, named twice
decisions.reason: "Roasted grain" appears twice in the list. It may have been copied twice by mistake; the early Greek translation does not repeat it. Or the second may name roasted seeds of the beans and lentils just listed. Either way roasted grain was among the gifts.

decisions.choice: bedding: beds or sleeping mats
decisions.reason: The word means a place to lie down. In this list it means bedding or mats for the weary company.

decisions.choice: basins and potter's vessels: bowls and clay pots
decisions.reason: These were the ordinary dishes and pots needed to cook and eat.

decisions.choice: the list is the object of "brought" in verse 29
decisions.reason: The verb comes only in verse 29, after all the goods have been named.

decisions.choice: brought
decisions.reason: Balanced moves the verb "brought" up to the start of the list, as English needs, and leaves out the repeated "roasted grain" (see m1); verse 29 does not repeat the verb.

decisions.choice: They brought ... They also brought
decisions.reason: Readable puts the list in short sentences of its own and lists roasted grain once.

records.source: וּדְבַ֣שׁ וְחֶמְאָ֗ה וְצֹאן֙ וּשְׁפ֣וֹת בָּקָ֔ר הִגִּ֧ישׁוּ לְדָוִ֛ד וְלָעָ֥ם אֲשֶׁר־אִתּ֖וֹ לֶאֱכ֑וֹל כִּ֣י אָמְר֔וּ הָעָ֗ם רָעֵ֛ב וְעָיֵ֥ף וְצָמֵ֖א בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃
records.gloss: And honey and curds and sheep and cheese of [the] herd, they brought for David and for the people which [was] with him to eat; for they said, the people [is] hungry and weary and thirsty in the wilderness.
pieces: honey and curds, sheep, and cheese from the herd, as food for David and the people with him. They said, "The people have become hungry and tired and thirsty in the wilderness."

L.29: and honey and curds and sheep and cheese of the herd. They brought [these] for David and for the people who [were] with him to eat, for they said, "The people [are] hungry and weary and thirsty in the wilderness."

R.29: And they brought honey, curds, sheep and cheese from cows. All this was for David and his people to eat. The men said to themselves, "These people must be hungry, tired and thirsty out in the wilderness."

decisions.choice: cheese of the herd: a product of cow's milk
decisions.reason: The first word occurs only here. It seems to name cheese or thickened cream made from the milk of cattle.

decisions.choice: they said: they thought
decisions.reason: "Said" here may mean that they said it to one another or that they thought it. Their words give the reason for their gifts.

decisions.choice: hungry, weary and thirsty in the wilderness
decisions.reason: The words may recall Israel in the wilderness, hungry and thirsty, where God provided for his people (Exodus 16-17). Here the provision comes through men east of the Jordan, one of them an Ammonite.

decisions.choice: curds: thickened milk
decisions.reason: The word names curdled milk or soft butter, a common food (Genesis 18:8; Judges 5:25).

decisions.choice: said to themselves; must be
decisions.reason: Readable takes "said" as what they thought (see m2) and adds "must be" to show it was their judgment.

decisions.choice: They brought [these]
decisions.reason: Literal starts a new sentence at the verb that completes the list of verses 27-28.
